issues.issue: The term takes its meaning from "the Guarantee Agreement", singular, but the defined term is "Guarantee Agreements" and there are two (Exhibit E-1 for EGL and E-2 for the Parent). Which instrument supplies the release date is not stated.

After four named contracts the definition sweeps in "any other material contract entered into by the Borrower with respect to any engineering, procurement or construction services", with no threshold for materiality. The reach of the catch-all against the enumerated specifics is open.

The Borrower must deposit "all Cash and receivables arising out of any contracts of the Borrower with any Person or payments otherwise received by Borrower", a sweep with no carve-out and no stated boundary. Its width against the Borrower's working-capital needs is left to construction.

Amounts in the Escrow Account are said to be applied "in accordance with the Cash Sweep Mechanism", yet Section 2.05 directs all loan advances into the same Escrow Account for disbursement to the Borrower for its Borrowing Request purposes. The two uses of one account are not reconciled here.

The definition omits the operative verb — "'Existing Credit Agreement' the Credit Agreement dated September 22, 2010" — leaving a sentence fragment. The meaning is recoverable but the drafting slip is on the face of the text.

"Financial Closure" requires Total Commitments of US$530,000,000 and Supplier Financing "made available" of US$182,750,000, but says nothing about who must procure them or what "made available" requires. The trigger for the Tranche B facility therefore rests on an unallocated and unmeasured condition.

The definition can only be satisfied if Subsequent Project Lenders accede under Section 2.20, which is discretionary, yet the Recitals state that term loan lenders "shall provide" US$530,000,000 and Section 2.02(b) makes the Initial Lender's own Tranche B available only after Financial Closure. Read together the Borrower's access to committed money depends on an event no party is bound to bring about.

A long list of specific events closes with "or other similar acts beyond the reasonable control of the Borrower", a general catch-all whose reach against the enumerated specifics is the classic ejusdem generis question. The 90-day/consultant qualifier adds a second undefined gate.

The definition extends to "related proceedings thereto that may be filed elsewhere in Federal or state court", an open-ended addition to a specifically identified action. Which future proceedings are "related" is left undetermined.

The list of hedging types closes with "or other derivative transaction of any kind or nature", an unbounded catch-all sitting against the named categories. Because Indebtedness includes all Hedging Agreement obligations, its width has real consequences.

Limb (f) sweeps in "any put options, shortfall undertakings, letters of comfort or any obligation undertaken by such Person in the nature of a payment obligation", a catch-all far wider than the specific debt categories preceding it. Whether ordinary contractual payment obligations become "Indebtedness" is genuinely arguable.

The Intercreditor Agreement is defined only as one "in form and substance satisfactory to the Borrower and the Required Lenders", with no terms fixed — an agreement to agree on the instrument that is to rank the secured parties. Nothing in the definition says what happens if satisfaction is withheld.

The term is defined as a "one-time request", while Section 2.07 is headed "Interest Elections" and speaks of an election operating for the initial and all subsequent Borrowings. Whether any later election is possible is unclear on the two texts together.
